status: captured (home, how-it-works, find-installer), judged by 2 combined AI jurors and the owner

entries.sector_note: The owner filed it under health; it is home climate hardware (ductless heat pumps) sold through installers. Filed as home.

business.what: Premium ductless heat pump system (indoor unit, outdoor unit, dial, app), installed by certified HVAC partners across North America.
business.action_that_pays: Find an installer (address form → local quote); no price on the site

claims.claim: Colour play across the site is harmonious, not monotonous
claims.evidence: 4 chromatic values in 2 hue families (teal/light blue, coral/salmon) on cream and white; coloured frames and blocks repeat them. The installer page uses no colour at all; teal links fail contrast (3.48:1).

claims.claim: Product photo slider with a description underneath explains the product; depends on the right photos
claims.evidence: Thumbnails switch photos of the four parts with one caption below. The caption names the part, not what the homeowner gains.

claims.claim: The vector graphics are made in tune with the site, creating harmony, not just present
claims.evidence: Isometric rooms drawn in the site's own palette and black line, with a temperature badge per room: the drawing explains room-by-room control. The inspector counted 0 illustrations on the home page (likely Lottie or late rendering): a measurement gap.

claims.claim: The 'Why homeowners love Quilt' section in a Pinterest layout is clever and uncommon
claims.evidence: Masonry of customer homes captioned by situation (office, houseboat, mobile home) in coloured frames. Masonry testimonial walls are common; the situation captions are what make it work. Quotes have no name or place.

claims.claim: A section with only a photo and an animated panel on the right is interesting
claims.evidence: The orange panel is a kinetic-type video repeating a slogan ('Better climate by design'): atmosphere, not information; adds page weight.

copy.copycheck: 354 words, 34 sentences, average 10.4 words; FAIL self-praise ('industry-leading')
copy.juror: About grade 9-11 (estimate). Voice calm and design-led, but superlatives stacked and three efficiency claims that do not match ('most efficient', 'most efficient 2- and 3-zone', '20% more efficient'). Unexplained jargon: SEER2, zones, ductless/mini-split. No cost, rebate or tax-credit signal.

library_candidates: Illustration drawn in the page's own palette and line, explaining the mechanism (rooms at different temperatures)
Product photographed as furniture in a room, with a press quote (Wirecutter) on the first screen
Customer homes captioned by situation (houseboat, mobile home, office) in frames of the brand colours
One sticky action in the header for the whole page ('Find an installer'); the paying form asks only for an address
avoid: A second audience's button ('Become a partner') at equal weight beside the homeowner's action
Superlatives and efficiency claims that contradict each other; unexplained trade jargon
The brand line living only inside a video; no h1; teal links and white hero text below AA
Scroll animations that ignore reduced motion (10 on the home page, 305 on How it works)

owner_taste_signal: Closest AI-owner agreement so far (6.7 vs 7.5). Second site the owner praises for colour with only 2 hue families (Quite Nice 9, Quilt 7): the owner reads 'colour play' as harmony across sections and illustration, not as the number of hues. The colour dial measures hue families; that may be the wrong measure (proposal, not changed).
